title: Jellyfish UFO Video: Amid Pentagon's Silence Harvard Astrophysicist Avi Loeb Says It Could Be A … [WATCH]
excerpt: Nothingburger or something worth noting? Harvard astrophysicist gives his take on the viral jellyfish UFO video that allegedly hovered over an US military base in Alaska.
content:
A video of a jellyfish-shaped UFO (unidentified flying object) has been all the buzz recently. Harvard astronomer Avi Loeb has now weighed in on the UAP (unidentified anonymous phenomenon). Loeb, who heads the White House's UAP Science Advisory Council, shared a clip of his interview about the footage on X/Twitter. Reacting to the viral UFO clip he said it could be the remnant of a balloon. He added that this is only a possibility, since objects like it have appeared in earlier videos and none has been effectively explained. FYI, the US Department of War has put out seven tranches of such material over the past five months, and the astrophysicists have reacted to quite a few of the content, including the UAP seen in the Apollo mission’s trove of data.

Loeb said the All Domain Anomaly Resolution Office at the Pentagon has classed these objects as unidentified. He had visited the office a few days ago. Officials there told him the data is not good enough to work out what the objects are, and he said the same applies to the jellyfish UFO.

Alleged Jellyfish UFO Seen Over Alaska pic.twitter.com/yOS4tyVLFH

— Professor Avi Loeb (@ProfAviLoeb) November 15, 2026

Three kinds of UFOs

According to Loeb, the released footage in the UFO Disclosure project by the US government shows three types: jellyfish-like objects, orbs, and triangular objects. The orbs are spherical blobs of light that, in his words, do not resemble drones. He said he wants new telescopes and observatories built to study them. The aim is a high-resolution image and a spectrum that would reveal what the objects are made of.

On how the military should respond to an unknown object moving blazing fast, Loeb said one from an adversarial nation can be shot down, as the Chinese spy balloon was in 2023. He added that civilians who film strange objects in the sky may be capturing data useful to the Pentagon. "The mystery remains," Loeb said.
